A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ElasticMM and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B. The material can be matched despite figure redesigns, pagination changes, and the added checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original serving-performance experiments, component ablations, and output-consistency results across 1,000 prompts in Appendix B.9.

after.justification: v3 reports serving-performance comparisons including DistServe, retains the ablations, and includes the original 1,000-prompt output-consistency experiment.

M1.justification: The load balancing, elastic scheduling, prefix caching, and non-blocking encoding procedures remain unchanged. Renaming 'Elastic Instance Allocation' to 'Stage Allocation' does not alter its steps or gain-cost equations.

E1.justification: Both versions use ShareGPT-4o and VisualWebInstruct for the same multimodal/text-only serving workloads, mixed-source ablations, and output-consistency evaluation. Multi-node evaluation remains future work.

E2.justification: The principal decoupled comparator changes from v2's custom vLLM-Decouple, described as separating request types without separating computation stages, to a multimodal DistServe extension that separates decode from colocated encoding/prefill. DistServe replaces that comparator in Figure 5 and joins vLLM in Figure 6; this is more than renaming.

E3.justification: The evaluated models, eight-A800 testbed, request generation, latency metrics, and SLO protocol remain unchanged. The 1–5 SLO scaling range newly repeated in Section 4.1 was already specified in v2's Section 4.2 and figures.

E4.justification: Both retain the static-allocation comparisons, incremental caching/non-blocking-encoding ablations, and Appendix B.9 output-equivalence check. The redesigned Figures 7–8 do not introduce new analytical questions or findings.

E5.justification: v3's new checklist item 7 claims that supplementary materials explain error bars and their calculation, but neither supplied PDF provides those details or identifiable error bars. The fixed-seed determinism statement in Appendix B.4 is unchanged, so the claimed uncertainty-reporting change cannot be verified.

E6.justification: Figure 5 now attributes the second latency series to DistServe rather than vLLM-Decouple, and Figure 6 adds DistServe throughput results for both models. Section 4.2 newly reports up to 2.3× throughput versus DistServe, although the plotted peak ratio is approximately 2.5×. The retained vLLM/ElasticMM throughput results, ablations, and Table 2 values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The scheduling equations and Appendix B's definitions, equivalence theorem, six lemmas, numerical-stability proposition, and proofs are retained without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same EMP contributions and headline claims of up to 4.2× lower TTFT and 3.2–4.5× throughput versus vLLM. Shortened contribution bullets preserve their scientific meaning.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes DistServe's high-load output latency to decode-node memory contention under static allocation. Section 6 expands the existing single-node limitation by identifying inter-node communication latency and a broader parallelism search space as unresolved challenges.

D1.justification: The new checklist states that code will become publicly available shortly, adding release-status information without supplying a code location or reproduction commands. Appendix A's implementation details remain unchanged apart from the allocation-component terminology.

R1.justification: v3 adds FlexPipe as reference 60 and briefly discusses its dynamic pipeline parallelism for training. DistServe was already cited in v2; its new evaluated role changes comparison positioning without a broad related-work rewrite.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited prose edits, shortens contribution bullets, revises scheduling terminology, corrects system-name typos, and updates affiliations. It adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, while retaining the main section sequence and appendix organization.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a substantially redesigned, enlarged framework diagram. Figure 6 expands from a half-width two-method plot to a full-width three-method comparison. Figure 5 loses its reduction arrows, and Figures 7–8 receive revised legends, markers, and placement, substantially reorganizing the principal visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The DistServe comparison adds useful evidence against a prefill/decode-disaggregated system, while the redesigned framework diagram and fuller multi-node discussion improve clarity. These are focused gains rather than a broader scientific advance. The unsupported checklist assertion about error bars and the discrepancy between the new 2.3× statement and Figure 6's approximately 2.5× peak temper, but do not outweigh, those improvements.
